batch_strategy: Measure small solvent-by-loading panels where existing labels show endpoint-specific behavior, add local anchors for adsorbing aromatic families, and repeat three conditions that discriminate reproducible curvature from label variation. Use the supplied predictions as frozen premeasurement baselines; treat CW distance and quantile spans as secondary evidence.

choices.reason: m84 at 20/1 and 59.35 mg anchors the approach to its weak-eluent completion rise. Measured 40/1 labels 0fb4ba3b33f8740a6a8a and f159b69487cebc7dcf97 differ substantially by loading; this point and the selected 30/1 point test where that response develops.

m84 at 30/1 and 59.35 mg fills the solvent gap before measured 40/1. Its predicted 7.35/19.28 mL can be tested against the measured low-load 40/1 completion of 19.20 mL in 0fb4ba3b33f8740a6a8a, distinguishing a plateau from a misplaced response knee.

Repeat m84 at 40/1 and 118.7 mg. f159b69487cebc7dcf97 measured 6.895/24.105 mL with historical V2 underprediction of 6.72 mL; the current forecast is 7.01/21.02. Repetition tests whether the higher completion is reproducible before transferring a loading correction.

m82 at 2/1 and 51.45 mg forms the low-load corner of a matched 1/1–2/1 panel. The predicted 8.09/15.51 mL tests whether the large loading dependence measured at 5/1 in 3ca8d2ff798fad4faffc already appears under stronger eluent.

m82 at 2/1 and 154.35 mg completes the matched loading contrast. QGeoGNN predicts only a small completion change relative to the selected low-load row, whereas the measured 5/1 pair 3ca8d2ff798fad4faffc and cd2c80dae2f32a52732f differs by about 7.08 mL in V2.

m82 at 1/1 and 51.45 mg supplies the strong-eluent baseline for the selected low-load 2/1 point. Together with the higher-load pair, it locates the emergence of solvent-dependent loading effects rather than assuming the measured 5/1 response applies throughout.

m82 at 1/1 and 154.35 mg completes the two-by-two panel. Predictions at both solvent ratios largely preserve V2 across loading; measuring this corner tests that assumption independently of the substantial 5/1 completion difference in 3ca8d2ff798fad4faffc and cd2c80dae2f32a52732f.

m168 at 50/1, 40 mg and 400 uL DCM tests transfer of the low-load onset anomaly measured with 300 uL DCM in 5f02dc3c13f7f2daed32. Current prediction is 6.38/25.05 mL versus that measured 10.57/26.83 mL at the other loading-solvent volume.

m168 at 50/1, 120 mg and 400 uL DCM pairs with the selected 40 mg row. Measured 300 uL rows 5f02dc3c13f7f2daed32 and e82a87ee526fdd9b1e8d show markedly different onset and completion loading responses; this pair tests their dependence on loading-solvent volume.

m168 under pure EA, 120 mg and 400 uL DCM completes a solvent/loading rectangle with measured 00ae0f7f3fc62795a036 and the selected weak-eluent pair. The measured low-load pure-EA V2 was 15.0 mL; this tests whether that baseline changes with loading.

m166 at 10/1 and 50 mg predicts 5.71/27.61 mL, placing completion above its measured low-load 20/1 value of 22.92 mL in 7ac16a6d90180a350ff0. This tests a possible local maximum and contrasts with higher-load 10/1 evidence 20acd2ae49790ab82053.

Repeat m92 at 2/1, 115.5 mg in 200 uL EA. f7d6c68ef2b3f637bd05 measured V2=10.325 mL, below both neighboring-load labels 9768d61b571fc0c5ce1a and b7880e59ff4586b29a28. Current prediction is 17.07 mL; repetition tests whether this loading minimum persists.

m202 at 2/1 and 122.3 mg bridges measured 1/1 and 5/1 anchors 87a651fc86ed976bd374 and 86258f5c8ffdb874521f. Its predicted V2=9.80 mL lies below both measured completions. This tests a local reversal for the explicitly cationic phosphorus structure; CW distance is also high at 0.963.

m202 at 1/1 and 183.45 mg tests the strong-eluent loading baseline against measured 87a651fc86ed976bd374. The extreme loading contrast measured at 10/1 in 902937db42f82f467718 and cb446680f62351d087a9 makes it useful to determine whether divergence is confined to weaker eluent.

m205 at 1/1 and 49.5 mg extends measured strong-eluent loading anchors 2b10c90b32f970e4b4c8 and 1aceeb0ee0419209d1c7. It connects those baselines to the low-load 5/1 condition 7954bf73f74c7fbcecb2, which historically had a 32.10 mL V2 underprediction.

m206 at 1/1 and 50 mg pairs directly with measured 2/1 low-load anchor 7c0c324643799c918828. It locates the strong-eluent transition for a naphthylmethanol and tests transfer from measured 1/1 at 100 mg, 53ceb391785085223695, without importing its weak-eluent historical error.

Quinoline m216 under pure EA at 54.65 mg begins a matched low-load solvent sequence with the selected 1/1 point and measured 2/1 row 5097ef8f92148f920ca4. The 5.03 mL V1 quantile span supports probing this baseline, but does not establish epistemic uncertainty.

m216 at 1/1 and 54.65 mg completes the strong-eluent pair. Measured 100 mg baselines ae187d6f3746213b630c and bea7a84fdcea344896f4 contrast with much later weak-eluent retention; this label tests loading dependence before that steep rise.

Nitroacetophenone m37 at 1/1 and 134.5 mg starts a matched solvent pair with 2/1. Its predicted completion is 16.92 mL, compared with measured 30.63 mL at 5/1 in 9de8f9fed06ef9d5befa. This locates the early part of the nitrocarbonyl response.

m37 at 2/1 and 134.5 mg tests the predicted near-plateau in V2 between 1/1 and 2/1 before the measured rise at 5/1 in 9de8f9fed06ef9d5befa. The matched pair separates solvent curvature from loading, while its high CW distance supplies an additional coverage signal.

Nitrobenzaldehyde m193 at 1/1 and 149.6 mg provides a structural contrast to the m37 pair and measured ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde 1/1 anchor e6326a07ad46fdd2e66f. It tests whether the predicted earlier completion for this aldehyde is appropriate.

Methyl anthranilate m104 under pure EA at 58.4 mg extends its measured low-load 1/1 and 2/1 anchors 3b06e84c0031a956a438 and a2b3a77e1b5200f7c164. An ortho amino–ester arrangement may alter accessible silica interactions; the label tests that prior at the solvent boundary.

Ethyl para-aminobenzoate m86 under pure EA at 58.5 mg tests whether its large measured 5/1 retention in c70b471334f9747d6f98 collapses at stronger eluent. Measured meta-isomer pure-EA row 0f80a7406c8b375d325b supplies a related structural reference.

Para-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 2/1 and 50 mg tests loading sensitivity before its steep 5/1 rise. Compare measured 100 mg 2/1 row 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f with the 5/1 loading contrast ad833f34f6b91872362d and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90.

Donor/acceptor-free m3 at 10/1 and 100 mg tests a predicted V2 maximum of 18.64 mL between measured 5/1 and 20/1 completions of 12.57 and 14.17 mL in c59ffcab9329339d3e91 and c25aed72c162a62800ce. The maximum remains unmeasured.

m3 at 50/1 and 100 mg completes a matched weak-eluent test of the predicted 10/1 maximum. The forecast falls to V2=12.79 mL despite weaker eluent; measuring both points tests whether this curve generalizes appropriately within low-polarity aromatic rows.

m32 at 2/1 and 50.2 mg tests loading transfer from the latest 150.6 mg label 05a6276f67b3cca8cc7f, whose onset was earlier and completion later than forecast. The new low-load anchor helps determine whether that endpoint pattern persists across loading.

m87 at 5/1 and 110.3 mg fills the loading midpoint between measured c449ecc5ee6acf61bddb and c1b9b6fc781ab8519301. Their V2 values rise from 13.43 to 17.47 mL while onset changes little; this label constrains a scaffold-specific completion response.

Repeat m174 at 30/1 and 164.55 mg. Measured 34cf0942ff52b1b80385 gives 16.06/27.00 mL, below both 20/1 row 591b1bb527d42e831f12 and 50/1 row cbedf4ab0af735b39b3a. Repetition tests the reproducibility of an observed solvent minimum.

m13 at 1/1 and 56.1 mg begins a matched low-load test of the completion decrease measured at 112.2 mg between 1/1 and 2/1 in 9e94f0a4a224512b06cc and 6573d8f84faaf7ce4a78. This tests whether the curvature survives a loading change.

m13 at 2/1 and 56.1 mg completes that solvent pair. Predicted V2 decreases from 20.30 to 17.56 mL, whereas measured low-load 5/1 row 1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23 finishes at 40.10 mL. The pair distinguishes a local minimum from a misplaced transition.

Methyl naphthylacetate m98 at 2/1 and 114.2 mg adds a transition anchor near higher-load 1/1 and 5/1 observations 4d7ac91993f7287406c8 and a4d269310b605d198465. Its high CW distance and 4.56 mL V2 quantile span support coverage of this ester neighborhood.

hypotheses.content: Loading responses depend on scaffold and solvent ratio, and can move onset and completion differently. Existing weak-eluent loading effects should not be transferred unchanged into stronger-eluent conditions or across loading-solvent volumes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched panels teach separate V1 and V2 responses to loading and identify where solvent or loading-solvent volume changes those responses. These interactions can generalize across numerous condition variants in the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m82 loading effect emerge between 1/1, 2/1 and 5/1, and does the m168 weak-eluent onset pattern persist when loading-solvent volume changes from 300 to 400 uL?

hypotheses.content: Completion curvature is local to scaffold and loading. The measured m13 completion decrease between 1/1 and 2/1 and the differing carbonyl response curves justify testing individual turning points rather than applying a common carbonyl correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local solvent anchors distinguish real endpoint curvature from transferred response shapes and constrain relationships among ketones, aldehydes, esters and multifunctional carbonyl compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m13 completion decrease persist at lower loading, does m166 have a low-load maximum near 10/1, and where do nitrocarbonyl completions begin rising under stronger eluent?

hypotheses.content: Large historical errors for aromatic nitrogen and hydroxyl-containing compounds are localized in condition space. Their strong-eluent baselines and the solvent strength at which retention rises require scaffold-specific and loading-specific anchors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Strong-eluent and low-load measurements can prevent a previously large weak-eluent correction from spreading into early-elution regions, while teaching structural differences in the onset of stronger silica retention.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do quinoline, the two naphthyl alcohols and amino aromatic esters retain their predicted strong-eluent baselines at the selected lower loads?

hypotheses.content: Labels at identical recorded conditions can differ substantially. Consequently, some apparent response discontinuities remain reproducibility or omitted-variable questions rather than established chromatographic mechanisms; selected repeats can characterize this ambiguity but cannot identify absent variables.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A few targeted repeats can indicate whether unusual labels represent recurring conditional behavior or variable outcomes, improving the evidence used to learn deterministic response surfaces without inventing missing experimental covariates.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the m84 higher-load late completion, m92 intermediate-load low completion and m174 solvent minimum reproduced at their recorded conditions?

hypotheses.content: The predicted m3 completion maximum near 10/1, followed by lower completion at 50/1, may represent either genuine local curvature or inappropriate transfer from other structures. Its turning point is currently unmeasured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched test on a donor/acceptor-free aromatic scaffold checks solvent-curve transfer outside polar failure regions and can constrain predictions for related low-polarity rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do measured m3 completions at 10/1 and 50/1 support the predicted maximum when loading and loading-solvent conditions are held fixed?

feedback_interpretation: The latest batch weakens the case for another broad retention correction. Many strong-eluent and low-polarity anchors were close to their acquisition forecasts, including m188 under pure EA, m113 under pure EA and m149 at 20/1. The largest recent completion miss was m84 at 40/1: V2 was underpredicted by 6.72 mL while onset was close. m32 at 2/1 showed earlier onset and later completion than forecast, with V2 underprediction of 4.91 mL. Conversely, m188 at 20/1 and low-load m192 at 5/1 had completion overprediction. These opposite signs strengthen local solvent/loading learning and weaken a universal positive V2 offset. The new m168 pure-EA label at 40 mg and 400 uL DCM finished at 15.0 mL versus 13.21 mL at the measured 300 uL condition; this motivates a matched volume/loading test, but one comparison does not establish a causal volume effect. I follow the observed-table mapping: c6924324ddd95f249df6 is m107, not the m26 assignment in its historical prose. Historical acquisition errors are trajectory evidence, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates measurements into interpretable local experiments. The m82 two-by-two panel and m168 panel test solvent, loading and loading-solvent-volume interactions separately for onset and completion. m84, m87 and m32 extend recent endpoint-specific feedback into neighboring conditions. The m13 pair, m166 anchor and nitrocarbonyl points test local curvature and response thresholds; m98 adds a related ester transition. Strong-eluent measurements for quinoline, naphthyl alcohols and amino aromatic esters delimit previously difficult adsorption regions without assuming their historical errors persist everywhere. Three repeats assess specific unusual labels or minima, motivated by genuine same-condition discrepancies elsewhere in the observations. The matched m3 pair supplies a low-polarity test of a predicted turning point, where the last batch's generally modest errors argue for a focused experiment rather than extensive additional controls. Together these labels should improve generalization by teaching conditional response shapes and limiting unsupported transfer across scaffolds. The 32 selections use distinct supplied candidate IDs and distinct molecule-condition tuples within the batch; there are no pending experiments.
